title: Project Finalization Audit
project: Hardware-Aware Data-Driven Testing and Fault Localization for Quantum Programs

limitations: Inventory and selected file contents were inspected; not every row of every CSV was independently recomputed.
Saved NPZ weights were schema-inspected but not loaded to reproduce predictions.
No fresh full-suite run was performed. Test totals in repository documentation are historical snapshots.

decision_rationale: The original project can be closed honestly with narrow claims about the implemented simulator, evidence-based rule diagnosis, dataset-specific binary QMutBench evaluation, and controlled simulator-only ML comparisons. The proposed 240-report wave is an optional new study, not a prerequisite for those claims. Its saved preflight is BLOCKED and it supplies no real-hardware validation.

implemented_and_tested: Statevector simulator, circuit API, supported gate execution, measurement, finite-shot sampling.
HardwareModel parameters for readout, gate calibration, coherence, and connectivity.
Distribution metrics and finite-shot anomaly comparison.
Evidence-based diagnosis with operation mismatch and calibration-backed hardware candidates; ambiguity and insufficient-evidence outcomes are supported.
High-level diagnose_circuit ideal/optional hardware-aware execution; lower-level diagnose_execution accepts distinct expected and observed circuits and distributions.
Observable feature extraction, adapter schema/probability checks, abstention, and independent localization gating are implemented; integration coverage uses mock classifiers.
not_implemented_or_not_verified: A compatible deployable observable-only three-class model artifact is not present; default ML inference intentionally raises ModelBackendUnavailable.
Real inference from a genuine compatible artifact is not verified by the mock-based adapter tests.
diagnose_circuit does not accept a separate reference circuit; use diagnose_execution for direct expected/observed comparison.
No real-hardware validation is present. IBM adapter validation is offline/fixture based; live backend access and execution are unavailable in checked-in status.

historical_suite_counts.context: latest verified full suite claimed; required writable pytest temp directory

best_supported_baseline.model: StandardScaler + LogisticRegression(C=1, max_iter=2000), fixed and unsearched

protocol.outer: 30-fold leave-one-circuit-family-out GroupKFold; each fold tests one full family (9 rows, 3 per class), with mutually disjoint outer test folds.
protocol.inner: 5-fold GroupKFold over the 29 outer-training families used for tuning candidate models; inner macro-F1 selection. Fixed logistic baseline is unsearched.
protocol.preprocessing: Scaler fitted inside training folds only; labels and family identifiers are targets/grouping metadata, not features.
protocol.holdout_overlap: No family overlap across any outer train/test split. Outer training sets overlap across folds.

best_supported_baseline.interpretation: Best fixed baseline for a predeclared comparable protocol; controlled simulator research evidence only. Nine rows per held-out family make per-family scores coarse. Exact feature collisions, limited families, and no significance test constrain conclusions.

tuned_candidate_not_validated_winner.protocol: Same nested 30-family outer evaluation; C chosen from predeclared values using inner grouped macro-F1.
tuned_candidate_not_validated_winner.interpretation: Highest pooled nested comparison score, but improvement is not consistent across families; do not call it a selected or validated winner.

label_and_feature_caveats: NORMAL labels are all original records and PROGRAM_FAULT labels are all mutant records, so record type and target are perfectly associated by construction.
All 211 original records have zero features; 1,258 mutant records also have zero features.
The later 1,675-row threshold-tuned held-out set is not the same size as the earlier 1,952-row test set; results and protocols must not be conflated.
This is preliminary dataset-specific binary classification, not independent program behavior truth or hardware-fault localization.

other_saved_evaluations.protocol: Hand-designed local rule-based diagnosis cases; no ML population estimate.
Small grouped controlled simulator evaluations and feature comparisons with saved predictions.
other_saved_evaluations.interpretation: Exploratory; low/unstable hardware separation, feature collisions, small/dependent splits; no real device evidence or reliable feature improvement claim.

model_artifact_status.incompatibility: Both NPZ files are binary NORMAL/PROGRAM_FAULT models over five trace features; production adapter expects ordered five observable distribution features and three classes including HARDWARE_ANOMALY.

scientific: QMutBench labels are record-type-derived, highly imbalanced, and not independent behavior ground truth.
All originals and many mutants have zero trace features, so dataset construction can drive apparent separation.
Three-class ML uses 30 controlled simulator families and synthetic hardware interventions; feature collisions occur and best-candidate hardware recall is 0.422.
Simulator channels/calibration are not physical device evidence; no real-hardware validation.
The 240-report proposal covers a narrow simulator subset and an exploratory four-family test only.
correctness_or_data_integrity: Ordinary sampled run reports do not expose per-shot gate_failed events for actual gate skips; traced path is a separate stream. This blocks realized skip-count reporting for the proposed wave.
Saved preflight reports no safe resumable, atomic, duplicate-safe, bounded bulk-run orchestration protocol for the proposed wave.
No concrete diagnosis misclassification or simulator defect was established in reviewed reports; this audit did not freshly execute the test suite.

first_wave.preflight_state: BLOCKED; decision STOP; no reports generated

blockers.detail: Actual sampled-stream RX gate skip events are not emitted/persisted; a separate stochastic trace cannot supply the realized count.
Safe isolated output, atomic writes, progress, resumability, duplicate handling, bounded retry/resource stop and reconciliation are unspecified.

first_wave.why_defer: Existing rule-diagnosis coverage and controlled grouped ML evidence support an honest bounded conclusion. The wave is needed only if a new narrow simulator study becomes a required claim; it will not establish real hardware performance or repair QMutBench label validity.

minimum_remaining_tasks.stop_condition: All summaries and conclusions state these limitations and do not imply physical hardware or production ML inference.

minimum_remaining_tasks.task: Index headline result citations to the exact saved report, predictions, manifest/model, labels and split protocol; keep 1,952-row and 1,675-row binary test protocols distinct.
minimum_remaining_tasks.stop_condition: Every cited result resolves to an existing artifact and identifies the protocol/caveat.

minimum_remaining_tasks.task: Keep first wave deferred/blocked; do not generate reports. If later promoted, separately resolve B1/B2 before any execution.
minimum_remaining_tasks.stop_condition: No reports, runner, code, or experiment added as part of this finalization.

minimum_remaining_tasks.task: Close project at this evidence boundary; do not connect the incompatible binary NPZ to the three-class adapter.
